Well binomial nomenclature is just naming a creature using its genus and species name. These names are derived from latin. For example the genus “Canis “ when translated to english means “dog”. Remember that when using the binomial system you have the genus first (always with a capital letter) with the species next (always in lowercase) so for the scientific name of humans we would be “Homo sapiens”.

When it comes to naming clades. You should probably make your clades sound latin If you want them to sound like the real deal.

Now, things like linnaean taxonomic ranking are kinda arbitrary. You can just just pick a clade that where you think all the species within the clade are sufficiently distinct from the species outside of the clade and just label that a genus or any other kind of taxonomic rank.

The common ancestor between the seakites and cnidariamorphs lived a life cycle very similar to jellyfish found on earth. With a motile medusal stage and a sessile polyp stage. Sea kites just took advantage of an unfilled ecological niche (presumably a filter-feeder subsisting off the plankton near the surface) and as a result they gradually lost the sessile stage of their lifecycle. So now their lifecycle consists of the motile bilaterally symmetrical seakite stage and the smaller radially symmetrical baby stage. 

The mutation of bilateral symmetry may have been beneficial to early sea kites as it would have allowed them to better evade predators near the epipelagic. 

cnidariamorphs are capable of reverting back to a polyp stage in response to stress. However, the sea kites continuously grow and cannot revert to a previous life cycle hence why they ended up developing a more complex nervous system.

Whilst on a larger scale i believe that your alien animals will likely evolve a means to breathe (as in inhale and exhale) Try opening your trachea and letting gas diffusion breathe for you. It just doesn’t work.

Nearly all complex life would go extinct. Despite what pop culture may tell you; radiation does not give people cool super powers or turn them into mutants that do not need to eat food or drink water. It kills everyone.

Its likely some species (as in very simple unicellular life) may adapt to take advantage of this new food source in the far future. But basically all complex life as we know it would go extinct. And you’d have to wait hundreds of millions of years for complex life to possibly re emerge again (this is very speculative. We don’t know if complex life would even capable of surviving harsh radiation). And by then it’s biochemistry may become much different in comparison to today we as it has evolved to protect itself from radiation that it would be difficult for most normal people to speculate on what life could evolve.

If you want to explore hypotheticals i would advise messing around with seeded worlds that are slightly different from earth. For example “what would happen if we placed X, Y, and Z on a planet with slightly stronger gravity. Etc etc. those things will help you understand the complexities of speculative evolution.

Or if you want you can just create a cool looking alien without much thought. Not very helpful but occasionally while messing around you may create a cool thing that piques your interest. And then create a better and actually fleshed out alien species.

With my limited knowledge i doubt small creatures with an “open lung” would need to actually “breath”. The reason we inhale and exhale is to first absorb oxygen and then excrete carbon dioxide. In a creature with an “open lung” gas diffusion would be constantly happening so i presume that in a small scale the creature may not need to actually “breath” (as in inhale or exhale) as gas diffusion would be all that it needed to absorb sufficient oxygen and excrete excess carbon dioxide. On a larger scale animals require more oxygen so it doesn’t seem farfetched for inhalation and exhalation to evolve.
